text: The four business requirement documents (Program v4, Epic 1 v4, Epic 2 v2, Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3), the P4 functional specification v3 and the P4 technical specification v3 are treated as the approved baseline for this PRD. No governance signature, Product Owner decision or FDA decision exists in the source documents, so the PRD is issued with status Draft and its approval table is left empty.
why: The playbook preconditions require a BRD whose status is Approved with a Product Owner decision in its governance table, and the D-RCV-60 overlay forbids waiting for approval. Without this assumption the run would stop, and the whole P4 requirement set would stay unrecorded.
read: Business Requirements Program v4 document control; Business Requirements Epic 1 v4 document control; Business Requirements Epic 2 v2 document control; Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 document control sheet; FSD P4 v3 document control (Status: In review); TSD P4 v3 document control (Status: In review)
applied_in: Front matter (status: Draft); section 1.1; section 13 (approval table empty); section 13.1
confirm: Product owner and the FDA at the requirements approval gate
impact: A different baseline version changes the requirement text this PRD quotes, not its structure; the caps, requirements and acceptance criteria keep their identifiers and their trace to REQ-ACA-nnn.

text: Where two sources disagree about who owns a behaviour, piece of data or path, the Microservice Ownership Map v1 ruling is followed and the R-PREC precedence of the Template and Rules is applied to the sources themselves. The loser is recorded as a gap row and the PRD states the owner it uses.
why: Architecture v5, the API Specification v4, the P4 technical specification and the P4 functional specification disagree on several P4 items, and a PRD that stayed silent would leave a reader unable to tell which owner applies.
read: Template and Rules v1 R3 (source precedence and default rulings) and R5.5; Microservice Ownership Map v1 rulings with ASM-A6-tables-1 to -15 and ASM-A6-api-1 to -8
confirm: Solution architect at the service contract review
impact: If a ruling is reversed, the affected capability moves back into this PRD as a requirement and out of the dependency list; the identifiers of the remaining capabilities do not change.

text: rwb-access keeps identity and session, roles, permissions, scope, masking, the delegation of authority table, the access log and break-glass. The reference-data load surface, the rule package registry and its six operations, the platform smoke workflow, the case record view, the list of values and the partner identity rows are outside this service and are recorded as dependencies only.
why: The Ownership Map moves four groups of behaviour out of P4 while the P4 functional and technical specifications still describe them, and a PRD cannot claim work another service owns without creating a duplicate backlog item and a duplicate acceptance set.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14, 20 and 41; Microservice Ownership Map v1 rulings ASM-A6-tables-3, ASM-A6-tables-5, ASM-A6-tables-6, ASM-A6-api-2, ASM-A6-api-3, ASM-A6-api-4 and ASM-A6-api-5; plan split_plan.json P4 slices
gap: CG-B-REQ-PRD-P4-1; CG-B-REQ-PRD-P4-2; CG-B-REQ-PRD-P4-3; CG-B-REQ-PRD-P4-4; CG-B-REQ-PRD-P4-14; CG-B-REQ-PRD-P4-15
applied_in: Section 2.4; section 5.1; section 6 (no FR for the moved behaviour); section 9; section 10.4; section 12
confirm: Solution architect and the owners of rwb-case, rwb-decision, rwb-partner and the platform library
impact: Reversing one item adds one capability and one to three requirements to this PRD and removes one dependency row; the release slices and the traceability to REQ-ACA-nnn are otherwise unchanged.

text: The authorise request carries the requested capability area, the right, the case reference where a case is named, and the caller's case facts (owner, queue, team, region); the answer carries the decision, the capability area, the right, the scope applied, the matrix version, the conflict version and a masked or clear marker per personal field ID. A refusal is a 403 with MSG-P4-002; a case outside the scope is a 404 with MSG-P4-003.
why: Architecture v5 names the authorise path and its three inputs and no source gives a request or answer schema, so every consumer fake and the whole wave 1 contract depend on a fixed default.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 41; TSD P4 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD P4 A2.1, A2.5, A2.14, A2.30 and the acceptance criteria AC-EXC-P4-005-01 and AC-ALT-P4-005-02
applied_in: Section 6 FR-P4-006, FR-P4-011, FR-P4-013, FR-P4-015; section 9.1; section 11 AC-P4-008, AC-P4-011
confirm: Solution architect at the service contract review, with the rwb-case and rwb-document contract owners
impact: A different field set changes the contract, the consumer fakes and the contract tests; the decisions the answer makes, the refusal codes and the rights model are unaffected.

text: The masking answer names a personal field ID with a masked or clear marker and never a rendering, the client renders the masked form of the field, and a masked caller never causes a clear value to be retrieved from the ACE PII path. A personal field with no masking row for any role is masked for every role.
why: The functional specification shows renderings (XXXX-XX-XX, XXXXXXXXX1234, XXXXXX5678) while the service must answer a marker, and the default for an unlisted field is stated only inside one exception acceptance criterion.
read: FSD P4 AC-ALT-P4-005-01, AC-EXC-P4-005-05 and AC-P4-007-01; TSD P4 T3.1 masking_rule (DF-REF-198 to 204); Non-Functional Specification v3 NFR-039 and NFR-040
applied_in: Section 6 FR-P4-016, FR-P4-017, FR-P4-018, FR-P4-019; section 8.1; section 11 AC-P4-012 to AC-P4-015
confirm: Compliance with the solution architect at the masking policy review
impact: A different marker vocabulary or a different default changes the contract field type and two tests; the per-role rule and the no-clear-fetch rule stay.

text: The authorise, masking and DoA answers are held in a cache that is refreshed when an AccessPolicyChanged or DoaLimitChanged event arrives, with a short time to live as a backstop. The time to live and the maximum staleness a consumer may see are not set by any source and are recorded as open.
why: Architecture v5 gives the authorise answer as cached and names two events for the cache refresh, and no source gives a payload, a window or a time to live, so without a default the refresh cannot be tested.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 43; Event and Messaging Design v4 (no row for either event); TSD P4 T5.3 ('None'); FSD P4 A2.3, A2.4 and A2.6
applied_in: Section 6 FR-P4-012, FR-P4-038; section 9; section 11 AC-P4-009, AC-P4-032
confirm: Platform event owner with the solution architect
impact: A published window changes the time to live and one integration test; the event names, the topic and the refresh behaviour stay as stated.

text: A break-glass grant lasts until the earlier of four hours and the end of the IAM group, the reason is between 20 and 1000 characters, and the activation requires an open incident, an IAM-approved grant, a capability area, a right and a scope. These values are the placeholders the P4 acceptance criteria carry until DL38 is answered.
why: DL38 records the access timers as values from the bank IAM standard that are not yet set and instructs placeholder values, while the only numbers in any source are inside the break-glass acceptance criteria.
read: FSD P4 AC-ALT-P4-009-01, AC-EXC-P4-009-02 and A2.10; TSD P4 API-P4-013; Decision Log v10 DL38 and DL01
applied_in: Section 6 FR-P4-028, FR-P4-030, FR-P4-031; section 11 AC-P4-024, AC-P4-026, AC-P4-027; section 12 Q-P4-05
confirm: SCB IT security with the security administrator
impact: A different duration or reason bound changes one parameter row and two tests; the approval, the marking of every action and the review stay.

text: The six-monthly access review produces a role holder list per role with holder, scope and date access was granted, and the file is delivered through rwb-integration as an outbound file. The interface row, the file pattern, the columns, the review-date convention and the recipient are not set by any source.
why: JOB-18 is the only scheduled work of the service and its artefact has no shape anywhere, so the requirement has to be stated at capability level with the artefact named and its layout marked open.
read: Architecture v5 slides 14 and 44 (JOB-18); Batch and Scheduling Design v4 JOB-18; TSD P4 T3.1 (no extract); FSD P4 A1.2 (no review feature); Architecture v5 slide 16 (deliverFile and the two delivery events)
applied_in: Section 6 FR-P4-033; section 9; section 10.3; section 11 AC-P4-029
confirm: Security administrator with the rwb-integration contract owner
impact: A different artefact or delivery path changes the file layout and the delivery call only; the six-monthly cycle and the recertification purpose stay.

text: The leaver response time and the access review interval are values of the bank IAM standard, to be read when DL38 is answered. This PRD states both as not specified in the source documents and does not choose a value.
why: DL38 holds both values as not a choice, and the P4 requirements carry no number, so inventing one would put an unapproved service level into the acceptance criteria.
read: Decision Log v10 DL38 ('Access timers: access review interval, leaver response time and break-glass review window'), DL39 and DL40; BRD Program v4 REQ-ACA-011; FSD P4 A2.13 and A2.10
applied_in: Section 6 FR-P4-032; section 11 AC-P4-028; section 12 Q-P4-05
confirm: SCB IT security with the security administrator
impact: The answer fills two parameters and one acceptance value; the joiner, mover and leaver behaviour and the review cycle are unaffected.

text: Wave 1 administers the permission matrix and the delegation of authority table by a validated file load with a valid-from date and a second-person approval, and the E8 administration screens add a self-service surface over the same data without changing the data model.
why: The Epic 1 requirements and acceptance criteria describe the policy change as a load with an approval, and the E8 features describe screens; without this reading the two would appear to be different capabilities with different data.
read: FSD P4 A2.4 AC-P4-005-01 and A2.6 AC-P4-006-01; FEAT-ADM-01, FEAT-ADM-03 and FEAT-ADM-06 with A2.17 to A2.22; BRD Epic 1 v4 RWB-E1-037 and RWB-E1-038; BRD Program v4 REQ-ACA-013 (Should, E8)
applied_in: Section 10.1 and 10.3; section 6 FR-P4-036 and FR-P4-037
confirm: Product owner with the security administrator
impact: If the screens replace the load rather than sit over it, the wave 1 slicing changes and FR-P4-036 moves earlier; the data model and the approval rule do not change.

text: Every date in this PRD is the date of the source document and is marked tentative: 30 November 2026 for wave 1, 31 December 2026 for wave 2 and 30 June 2027 for wave 4. No date is raised as a gap.
why: The run rules and DL48 keep the dates unchanged and tentative, and a date is never a gap; the wave to release map of the Template and Rules supplies the release of each business epic.
read: Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R1 U7, R5.6 and R8.2; Decision Log v10 DL48; BRD Epic 1 v4 (release 30 November 2026); BRD Epic 2 v2 (release 31 December 2026); plan split_plan.json release per business epic
applied_in: Front matter; section 1.2; section 10 and each increment title
confirm: Product owner at the release plan review
impact: A moved release date changes the three increment headings and no requirement.

text: rwb-access enforces the second factor and the scope for a partner identity that the partner gateway presents, answers the check and publishes nothing about the partner; the partner identity rows, the partner portal and the partner sign-in stay with rwb-partner. The partner identity attributes the answer needs are the partner firm and the partner role.
why: REQ-ACA-012 is a Must and the Ownership Map gives partner users and the portal to rwb-partner, so the P4 part of the requirement has to be stated without claiming the partner channel.
read: BRD Program v4 REQ-ACA-012; BRD Epic 2 v2 RWB-E2-019; Architecture v5 slide 20 (partner gateway in the DMZ, partner gateway to rwb-partner) and slide 41 (S9 owns partner users); Microservice Ownership Map v1 ruling ASM-A6-tables-6; Non-Functional Specification v3 NFR-050 and section 4
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-P4-11; section 6 FR-P4-034; section 9; section 10.2; section 11 AC-P4-030
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-partner contract owner at the DL03 answer
impact: If the partner identity is resolved in rwb-access instead, one capability and its requirement move into this PRD and the dependency row leaves section 9.

text: The values of the Non-Functional Specification v3 are the values this PRD is written against, with the status each one carries. A value marked Proposed is used as written until its owner confirms it under the decision named; a value marked Open is recorded as not set.
why: The non-functional specification states that a value marked Proposed is built and tested against the value shown until the owner confirms it, and several of its values are open under DL11, DL26 and DL27.
read: Non-Functional Specification v3 section 1 ('A requirement marked Proposed is built and tested against the value shown until the owner confirms it under the decision named') and section 5; TSD P4 T7
confirm: Solution architect with Risk at DL11
impact: A confirmed value replaces the target text in one NFR row; the requirement and its acceptance evidence keep their identifiers.

text: The third object of REQ-ACA-006, written as 'the data lake copy', is read as 'a data product', because Architecture v5 removes the data lake and the reporting read model is built from events into rwb-reporting. Nothing else in the requirement changes.
why: The requirement as written cannot be met once the data lake is removed, and leaving the wording unchanged in the PRD would make the access log requirement untestable.
read: BRD Program v4 REQ-ACA-006; Non-Functional Specification v3 NFR-042; Microservice Story Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-17; Architecture v5 slide 37
confirm: Compliance with the solution architect when REQ-ACA-006 is re-issued
impact: If the wording stands, FR-P4-023 keeps two objects and one test case is dropped; the access log itself is unaffected.
